skim: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo neared 3,800 deaths and spread toward the Central African Republic and South Sudan borders as Typhoon Surigae turned toward Japan’s mainland, threatening the Asian Games closing ceremony after a magnitude-7.0 quake rattled New Caledonia last week.

Trump wouldn’t rule out further Iran strikes even as Tehran’s Pezeshkian signalled openness to nuclear talks, while drone and explosive strikes hit Sudan’s Wad Madani and Nyala after Burhan was denied a US visa, and Gaza’s death toll topped 74,000.

Chinese open-weight models like DeepSeek and Qwen now handle up to two-thirds of global AI token usage, alarming Washington enough to trigger a congressional probe, as Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle its Siri AI delay lawsuit and Nadella pitched Copilot as a ‘new OS for work.’

Modi marked 10 years since the 2016 surgical strikes as the Cockroach Janta Party confirmed Oct 2 nationwide protests over the election chief, Andy Burnham pledged a free national care service at Labour conference, and Qatar condemned settler incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque.

Kohli and Gill scored centuries as India beat West Indies in their ODI opener, Qatar beat Yemen to reach the Gulf Cup semi-finals, Portugal survived a Haaland scare to beat Norway, and F1 teams await a mid-October call on the Qatar and Abu Dhabi season-closers.

stories.headline: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Spreads Across Borders as Death Toll Nears 3,800
stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths — a 48% fatality rate — with the virus now spreading into Bulu, near the Central African Republic border, and Dungu, near South Sudan, per Al Jazeera (Sep 25). WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said “it’s very difficult to see Ebola in isolation because even our response to Ebola is affected by the conflict,” while Africa CDC’s Dr. Jean Kaseya warned that with only 30,000 of roughly 420,000 expected contacts traced, “when the outbreak is at community level, we cannot talk about control.”

stories.headline: Typhoon Surigae Turns Toward Japan’s Mainland, Threatening Asian Games Closing
stories.body: Typhoon Surigae is churning north-northeast at 15 km/h with sustained winds of 35 m/s and gusts to 50 m/s, on track to approach Okinawa and the Amami Islands by Sep 29 before its track curves toward Japan’s Chubu region — including Aichi Prefecture — around Oct 1-2, just before the Asian Games closing ceremony on Oct 4, per SBS (Sep 27), citing the Japan Meteorological Agency. Forecasters caution the storm’s future path “remains fluid,” but warn “rain clouds from the typhoon could blanket the region” regardless of a direct hit.

stories.headline: Trapped in Russian-Occupied Oleshky, Ukrainians Face Starvation and No Way Out
stories.body: In Russian-occupied Oleshky, just 9km from Ukrainian-held Kherson, roughly 1,500 residents (including 40 children) are surviving on garden produce and bartered goods after all food deliveries stopped in May, with some reduced to eating dogs and weed soup as basic goods like salt sell for 1,000 rubles, per Meduza (Sep 27). Around 100 bodies have piled up in the hospital’s basement since May with no organized evacuation route open, and Tetiana Hasanenko, head of the city’s exiled Ukrainian administration, said “it’s a humanitarian catastrophe, people are driven to despair.”

stories.headline: EU Unlocks $810 Million in Aid for Africa, Ukraine and Gaza
stories.body: The European Commission pledged €710 million ($810 million) in humanitarian aid on Sep 27, split across sub-Saharan Africa migration and food-insecurity response (€477 million combined), Palestinian territories and Lebanon (€103 million), Ethiopia’s primary healthcare system (€60 million), Ukraine (€52 million), and €7.5 million toward the Ebola response in Congo, per Al Jazeera (Sep 27). Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said “conflicts, extreme weather events and rising living costs are throwing the lives of many people around the world into disarray.”

stories.headline: Kohli and Gill Centuries Seal India’s ODI Opener Over West Indies
stories.body: India chased down 296 to beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series-opening ODI at Thiruvananthapuram, with Virat Kohli unbeaten on 139 off 88 balls (11 fours, seven sixes) and captain Shubman Gill making 110. Left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav, whose 4/40 had restricted West Indies to 295, was named Player of the Match ahead of both centurions — a call he found “awkward,” saying, “I actually loved the batting from Shubman and Virat bhai, it was a special inning from them,” per Yahoo Sports (Sep 27).

stories.headline: Pakistan Through to Asian Games Semis as Rain Washes Out Hong Kong Tie
stories.body: Persistent rain wiped out Pakistan’s Asian Games quarter-final against Hong Kong in Nisshin without a ball bowled, sending Pakistan through to the semi-finals on their higher ICC T20I ranking — a day after a similar washout in Japan set up the India-Afghanistan tie, per IANS (Sep 28). Pakistan will face the winner of the Bangladesh-Malaysia quarter-final for a place in the final, with rain continuing to disrupt the men’s tournament.

stories.headline: Ramos Brace Sinks Norway as Ronaldo-Less Portugal Survive Haaland Scare
stories.body: Gonçalo Ramos struck twice as Portugal came from behind to beat Norway 2-1 in the Nations League, with João Félix opening the scoring before Erling Haaland’s 65th international goal levelled it, only for a series of Norwegian goalkeeping errors to gift Ramos his winner. Cristiano Ronaldo was absent from the squad entirely, and Ramos said afterwards, “The most important thing is to show what I can do whenever I’m called upon,” per Al Jazeera (Sep 27).

stories.headline: F1 Teams Await Mid-October Call on Qatar and Abu Dhabi Season-Closers
stories.body: Formula 1 team principals say they expect a final decision by mid-October on whether the season-closing Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix can proceed as scheduled in late November and December, with Italy’s Imola circuit on standby as a substitute and F1 pledging to cover any losses if it prepares in vain. Haas boss Ayao Komatsu said organisers are “targeting to tell us in mid-October,” while Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton said, “I personally want to go. I love going to the Middle East,” per Sky Sports (Sep 26).

stories.headline: Paramount Launches $7.5 Billion Debt Raise for Warner Bros. Deal
stories.body: Paramount Skydance began syndicating a $7.5 billion senior secured term loan, part of roughly $44 billion in fresh debt needed to close its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, per Reuters (Sep 24). The raise follows Paramount’s settlement of litigation with a coalition of U.S. states and the Writers Guild of America, in which it agreed to boost domestic film production and create an editorial-independence board for CNN and CBS — and once the merger closes, the combined company is expected to carry about $80 billion in debt.

stories.headline: Boeing Lands 111-Jet Orders as Airlines Clash Over China Routes
stories.body: Boeing secured orders for 111 aircraft from Turkish Airlines and Biman Bangladesh Airlines, a win President Trump credited to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, calling it a “big day” for manufacturing that would “support tens of thousands of American jobs,” per Benzinga (Sep 27). The same week, Airlines for America — representing Delta, United and American — pushed back on a White House proposal to expand US-China flight capacity, warning it would open “competitive gaps for US airlines.”

stories.headline: Trump Cancels $810 Million in Funding Via Rare ‘Pocket Rescission’
stories.body: The White House used a rarely invoked “pocket rescission” — timed so close to the September 30 fiscal year-end that Congress has no chance to review it — to cancel $810 million in previously approved funding across 11 pools, per Benzinga (Sep 26). The cuts hit $567 million in HHS social-services grants along with State Department academic fellowships, HUD housing-counseling programs and DOJ race-relations offices; it is only the second such maneuver by any administration in 49 years, and the Government Accountability Office has ruled the practice illegal, a view the administration disputes.

stories.headline: Chinese AI Models Now Dominate Global Usage, Alarming Washington
stories.body: Chinese open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Z.ai and Alibaba’s Qwen now account for 57-67% of token usage on developer platform OpenRouter, up from just 6-13% in February, prompting two House committees to investigate the shift, per CNBC (Sep 26). “Chinese models are becoming capable enough for more tasks at a much lower cost,” said Vercel’s Harpreet Arora, noting Chinese models processed two-thirds of tokens used by businesses across 82 “Global South” countries even as Nvidia, Meta and Microsoft have opposed sweeping new restrictions.

stories.headline: Apple to Pay $250 Million to Settle Siri AI Delay Lawsuit
stories.body: Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle a class-action lawsuit over the delayed launch of its overhauled Siri AI, with the claims site accepting submissions through December 21 and each eligible iPhone owner in line for an estimated $25 to $95, per MacRumors (Sep 26). Apple said it “denies all of the allegations made in the lawsuit” but chose to settle rather than face the cost and risk of a trial.

stories.headline: Medical AI Search Engine OpenEvidence Raises $250 Million at $15 Billion Valuation
stories.body: OpenEvidence, the clinical AI search engine used by more than 40% of US doctors across over 10,000 healthcare facilities, raised $250 million led by Andreessen Horowitz at a $15 billion valuation — up from $12 billion earlier this year — per Axios (Sep 25). The company, which offers its tool free to clinicians in the US and Canada, is fortifying its position in health care even as general-purpose AI giants push deeper into the sector.

stories.headline: Nadella: Microsoft Building Copilot as a ‘New OS for Work’
stories.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the company is building Copilot as “a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task,” unveiling a standalone “super app” built around four pillars — Home, Office apps, Code and the autonomous-agent layer Autopilot — per Windows Latest (Sep 26). The move comes even as Microsoft strips deep Copilot integration back out of Windows 11 itself, a pivot away from its earlier “agentic OS” framing that had drawn user backlash.

stories.headline: Trump Won’t Rule Out More Iran Strikes as Pezeshkian Signals Openness to Nuclear Talks
stories.body: A day after rejecting Iran’s seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Trump told reporters at the Presidents Cup “I think what’s going to happen is we’re going to win this war very soon,” declining to rule out further strikes: “it’s possible, but I just don’t want to say that,” per Fox News (Sep 27). Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian struck a softer tone on CBS’s Face the Nation, saying “we’re still talking, we’re still engaging in dialogue,” and on nuclear limits, “of course we agree. We had already reached an understanding on this in our previous talks,” while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi added “we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”

stories.headline: Drone and Explosive Strikes Hit Sudan’s Wad Madani, Nyala as Burhan Digs In
stories.body: A drone strike hit a fuel depot in Wad Madani and two explosions rocked Nyala in South Darfur, per Arab News (Sep 28), a day after the US denied army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan a visa to the UN General Assembly over his refusal to accept a three-month ceasefire with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Burhan told supporters “our goal is to eliminate this militia no matter how long it takes,” and “we do not want a visa from any country. We will stay here and die with you in this country,” arguing a truce would let the RSF regroup and rearm.

stories.headline: Gaza Death Toll Tops 74,000 as Netanyahu Holds Line on Full Hamas Disarmament
stories.body: Gaza’s Health Ministry reported the Palestinian death toll has surpassed 74,016, with 175,068 wounded, since the war began on Oct 7, 2023, including 1,145 Palestinians killed since the ceasefire took effect on Oct 10, 2025, per a report carried by WSLS (Sep 27). Israeli forces now hold more than half of Palestinian territory in Gaza, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said troops will not withdraw until Hamas disarms.

stories.headline: Venezuelans Rally in Four Cities for Machado’s Return, Elections
stories.body: Hundreds of supporters in sky-blue shirts marched in Caracas, Valencia, Maracaibo, and Merida on Sep 27 demanding the safe return of exiled Nobel laureate Maria Corina Machado and a path to presidential elections, per Al Jazeera (Sep 28), nine months after interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took over following Maduro’s removal by US special forces in January. Activist Flavio Valentini said “this is not a matter of parties or politics. This is a movement for the people and by the people,” while Vente Venezuela’s Anthony Romero said organizers “hope this transition process leads us to presidential elections and consolidates a free, democratic country.”

fixtures.headline: India vs West Indies, 2nd ODI
fixtures.body: India and West Indies move to Guwahati’s Assam Cricket Association Stadium for the second ODI of their three-match series, with India 1-0 up after Kohli and Gill’s Thiruvananthapuram centuries; the series concludes in New Chandigarh on Oct 3.

fixtures.headline: Asian Games Men’s Cricket Semi-Finals
fixtures.body: Pakistan have already booked a semi-final berth after their Hong Kong quarter-final washed out; they’ll meet the Bangladesh-Malaysia winner, with the second semi-final slot going to whoever emerges from the rain-hit India-Afghanistan and Nepal-Sri Lanka ties.

fixtures.headline: Bahrain Grand Prix at Sepang, Malaysia
fixtures.body: F1 returns to Sepang for the first time since 2017 when the relocated Bahrain Grand Prix runs Oct 2-4, with Kimi Antonelli holding a 50-point championship lead over Lewis Hamilton heading into the humid, rain-prone circuit.

fixtures.headline: Liverpool vs Manchester City
fixtures.body: Liverpool host Manchester City in the Premier League’s standout October fixture on a Sunday afternoon, one of several marquee games — including Man Utd vs Tottenham and Leeds vs Man Utd — picked for live TV in the weeks ahead, per Sky Sports.

portfolio.headline: Oppenheimer Lifts Microsoft Price Target to $570, Cites Azure Growth Outstripping Guidance
portfolio.body: Oppenheimer’s Brian Schwartz raised his price target on Microsoft to $570 from $515 on Sep 22, keeping an Outperform rating, after a management meeting left him projecting Azure’s constant-currency growth near 46% for the coming quarter, accelerating toward 50% the quarter after — with AI demand, he said, expected to keep outstripping available capacity through year-end (per Benzinga, Sep 22). He also pointed to strong Copilot subscription revenue and new AI-agent features as growth drivers heading into fiscal 2027.

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare Discloses Container-Isolation Flaw as Cybersecurity Valuations Get a Rethink
portfolio.body: Cloudflare disclosed a vulnerability in its Containers and Sandboxes products that could have let a customer recover residual disk data left behind by other customers on the same host; the company said it found no evidence of exploitation before patching it (per a StockStory report, Sep 25). The disclosure landed alongside a broader reassessment of cybersecurity valuations after the sector’s AI-driven run-up this year.

portfolio.headline: Apple’s $1,999 Foldable iPhone Duo Struggles to Define Its Buyer, Analysts Say
portfolio.body: Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the $1,999 iPhone Duo launched September 11, is on pace to sell nearly six million units by year-end but is projected to hold only around a quarter of the global foldable market against Samsung’s roughly 40% share, per Counterpoint Research figures cited by Yahoo Finance (Sep 27). Creative Strategies’ Carolina Milanesi and Counterpoint’s Neil Shah both pointed to a “lapse in positioning” — Apple has stayed vague about who the device is actually for — with foldables still expected to stay under 3% of total 2026 smartphone shipments.

portfolio.headline: Tesla’s Nevada Semi Plant Hits Volume Production as Einride, PepsiCo-Led Coalition Place Fleet Orders
portfolio.body: Tesla’s new Nevada Semi facility, built for up to 50,000 trucks a year, formally opened September 24 after its first unit rolled off the line in April, with logistics operator Einride ordering 500 trucks and a PepsiCo-led shipper coalition slated to take up to 2,500 more, per Yahoo Finance/TIKR (Sep 26). BNP Paribas Exane nonetheless cut its price target to $268 from $280, citing the EU’s self-driving vote slipping to December at the earliest and Musk’s comment that autonomy work is taking a “backseat” for six months.

portfolio.headline: Starbucks to Shutter 250 North America Stores, Book $300 Million Charge
portfolio.body: Starbucks will close roughly 250 “underperforming” stores across North America — about 1% of its ~18,000 locations there — and record a $300 million restructuring charge, with most closures completing by the end of fiscal 2026, per Yahoo Finance/InvestorsHub (Sep 24). It’s a separate action from CEO Brian Niccol’s earlier turnaround moves, which already carried roughly $1 billion in prior closure and roastery-shutdown charges.

portfolio.headline: Rolls-Royce Lands Philippine Airlines A350 Engine Order, Advances £1.4bn Nuclear Supply-Chain Push
portfolio.body: Rolls-Royce secured a contract worth “several hundred million pounds” to supply and service engines for nine new Philippine Airlines Airbus A350-1000s, while its SMR unit continues a £1.4 billion British supplier programme tied to its small modular reactor rollout, per Ad Hoc News (Sep 27). Bernstein raised its price target on the shares to 1,600 pence from 1,500 pence on the back of the order flow.

portfolio.headline: Ring Energy Guides to 10%+ 2027 Production Growth, Doubling Long-Lateral Drilling
portfolio.body: Ring Energy set a 2027 capital budget of $135–$165 million and guided to more than 10% year-over-year production growth, driven by doubling the number of horizontal wells with laterals longer than 1.5 miles across its Central Basin Platform acreage, per Yahoo Finance/MarketBeat (Sep 26). The company also targets roughly 1x leverage by year-end 2027 and says it would stay free-cash-flow positive even at $60-a-barrel oil, against a $75 base-case planning assumption.

stories.headline: Modi Marks 10 Years Since 2016 Surgical Strikes, Warns Terrorism Will Be Met With Force
stories.body: In his Mann Ki Baat radio address, PM Modi commemorated the 10th anniversary of India’s September 2016 surgical strikes across the Line of Control, launched after the Uri army camp attack. “India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a strong and decisive response,” Modi said, calling the strikes “a bold new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy” under a “zero tolerance” doctrine — per WION (Sep 27).

stories.headline: IIT Bombay Student’s Father Begins Hunger Strike at Azad Maidan
stories.body: Ravindra Wakode launched his sit-in fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Monday, alleging caste discrimination drove his 22-year-old son Sahil’s death at IIT Bombay on September 18. “I do not care, even if I get arrested. My son should get justice constitutionally,” Wakode said, vowing to continue fasting until those responsible are punished — per The Shillong Times (Sep 28).

stories.headline: Cockroach Janta Party Confirms Oct 2 Nationwide Protest After CEC Deadline Lapses
stories.body: With its 48-hour ultimatum for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation expiring September 26 unmet, the Cockroach Janta Party will launch a nationwide agitation from Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on October 2. “If Gyanesh Kumar does not resign… CJP will begin its nationwide protest from Mumbai on 2 October, and take it to cities across India,” said founder Abhijeet Dipke, with Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Aaditya Thackeray pledging solidarity and Congress holding its own demonstrations September 28 — per The Logical Indian (Sep 27).

stories.headline: India Rebukes Pakistan PM Sharif’s Kashmir Remarks at UN, Calls It an ‘Army-Run Regime’
stories.body: After Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif thanked US President Trump for “timely intervention” in the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict and pressed for a “just and fair solution” on Kashmir at the UN, India’s First Secretary Petal Gahlot hit back, branding Islamabad a “regime of the army, by the army, and for the army” and warning that “Pakistan’s terrorism, deceit and duplicity will neither benefit it” — per OnManorama (Sep 26).

stories.headline: Burnham Pledges Free, NHS-Style National Care Service at Labour Conference
stories.body: PM Andy Burnham used Labour’s Liverpool conference to pledge a universal, tax-funded social care overhaul for the next election manifesto, pushing back on suggestions it would cost £18bn a year: “It’s not that high.” “Somebody needs to grasp the nettle. I will be the one to do that,” he said, adding “it might make me unpopular with some, but that isn’t going to stop” him — per Newsbeep (Sep 27).

stories.headline: Court Clears Orange Order March Through Catholic Area of Portadown, Sparking Protests
stories.body: Northern Ireland’s High Court rejected a last-minute injunction bid, allowing the Orange Order to march down Portadown’s Garvaghy Road for the first time in 28 years, with the Parades Commission capping it at 35 marchers, no bands, finishing by 9:30am. Crowds linked arms to block the route as First Minister Michelle O’Neill said “I am calling for calm on all sides,” while Sinn Féin’s Mary Lou McDonald called the ruling “disgraceful” — per Al Jazeera (Sep 27).

stories.headline: Trump Expects Iran Talks to Resume This Week, With Doha in the Mix
stories.body: President Trump told Axios he expects indirect talks with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz standoff to resume as soon as Monday, after rejecting Tehran’s truce proposal: “They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make… They overplayed their hand.” Over 20 million barrels of oil transited the Strait over the weekend, and Trump did not rule out resuming strikes after the November 3 US midterms — per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 27).

stories.headline: Qatar Edge Yemen 1-0, Book Gulf Cup Semi-Final Spot
stories.body: Qatar backed up their Bahrain win with a second straight victory at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup in Jeddah, beating Yemen 1-0 through Yusuf Abdurisag’s 64th-minute strike, despite Akram Afif missing a penalty. The result sends the Asian champions into the semi-finals alongside the UAE — per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 27).

stories.headline: Qatar Condemns Settler Incursions Into Al-Aqsa Mosque
stories.body: Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally condemned Sunday’s settler incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque under Israeli forces’ protection, calling them violations of international law and affirming that “Al-Aqsa Mosque is an exclusive place of worship for Muslims” and that unilateral moves to alter Jerusalem’s status quo “are null and void.” Doha renewed its call for a Palestinian state on 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital — per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 27).

doha_events.headline: Doha Jewellery & Watches Exhibition Opens Its 22nd Edition
doha_events.body: DJWE 2026 runs September 28–October 3 at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre, with over 49 exhibitors and 500+ brands across dedicated Qatari, Turkish and Indian designer pavilions, plus a first-time participation from Christie’s. “The exhibition brings together a distinguished selection of international and regional brands alongside Qatari designers, providing a platform that celebrates exceptional craftsmanship and innovation,” said HE Saad bin Ali Al Kharji, Chairman of Qatar Tourism — per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 23).

doha_events.headline: Qatar Stars League Cup Second Round Kicks Off Across Doha
doha_events.body: The QSL Cup’s second-round matches run September 28, 29 and October 1 across venues including Al Sailiya SC, Grand Hamad Stadium, Al Khor Stadium and Hamad bin Khalifa Stadium, with tickets from just 10 QAR — per Pravasi News Daily (Sep 28).

doha_events.headline: Tasweer’s ‘Frame and Focus’ Photography Exhibition Runs Through Oct 5
doha_events.body: Twelve photographers who completed Tasweer’s 14-week advanced course showcase documentary and conceptual work on identity, memory and heritage at Al Hosh Gallery, The Pearl, through October 5. “Frame and Focus speaks to a wider ambition for photography in Qatar and the region,” said Tasweer director Khalifa Al Obaidly, while The VII Foundation’s Ziyah Gafić added that “telling your own story is a human right” — per The Peninsula Qatar (Sep 6).

doha_events.headline: Zinatha’s 8th Edition Brings Women’s Fashion to Al Hazm Mall
doha_events.body: The Zinatha exhibition returns for its 8th edition September 30–October 7 at Al Hazm Mall, with free entry to browse abayas, jalabiyas, beauty products and seasonal collections from designers across the GCC and wider Arab region — per Pravasi News Daily (Sep 28).
